LESSON: WRITING 2.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you make your composition interesting to read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions
2. create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 2.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
This lesson teaches Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing for Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing above.
2. Explain Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you make your composition interesting to read?
2. Why is it important to proofread your composition?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions
2. create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
